title: Derived tensor product
statement:
Fix primes $p\ne\ell$, an integer $a\geq1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a chosen algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ and a finite intermediate extension $\mathbf Q_\ell\subseteq E\subseteq\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme $X_0$. Put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$. Use the Weil complexes of [def-wf-weil-category] and its coefficient category $D^b_c(X,E)$, namely the rationalization [def-weil-pbc-rational-category] of the integral category specified there. Write $\Phi_X=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$, where $\gamma:z\mapsto z^{1/q}$ is the geometric Frobenius automorphism of $k$ [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. The notation $\Phi_X^*$ means the completed pullback followed by rationalization specified in [def-wf-weil-category]. In this scheme-automorphism case that node identifies completed pullback with coefficient transport, so the explicit inverse-image comparison below uses this same functor.

Here is the derived tensor convention, including the coefficient model implicit in $D(X,E)$. On a small ringed site $(\mathcal C,R)$, choose complexes $C,D$ representing $M,N\in D(R)$, and a quasi-isomorphism $P\to C$ with $P$ K-flat and with flat terms [def-pc-kflat-complex, lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Define
$$
 M\otimes_R^L N=Q_R\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_R D),
$$
where total tensor is [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] and $Q_R$ is localization at quasi-isomorphisms. Use the derived bifunctor obtained by localization [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]; thus this is computation by a K-flat replacement of the first argument, not a requirement of a functorial choice of complex representatives.

For the adic coefficient category above put $A=\mathcal O_E$, choose a uniformizer $\varpi$, and let $A_X=\varprojlim_n(A/\varpi^n)_X$ be the completed sheaf on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Write $D_{\mathrm{comp}}(A_X)$ for the full subcategory of $D(A_X)$ of objects whose completion map in [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion] is an isomorphism. The ambient notation $D(X,E)$ here means $D_{\mathrm{comp}}(A_X)[1/\varpi]$, using raw scalar localization [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization]. Its bounded constructible objects are the objects selected by [def-wf-weil-category], with its given proper-base-change integral definition. For integral representatives $M,N$ of arbitrary objects in this ambient rational category define the tensor construction by
$$
 M\mathbin{\widehat\otimes}_A^L N
   :=(M\otimes_{A_X}^L N)^{\wedge}_{\mathrm{Kos}},
$$
using the completion functor $D(A_X)\to D_{\mathrm{comp}}(A_X)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-completion-reflector], represented by the explicit Koszul mapping-fiber model of [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion]. Its rationalization is denoted $K\otimes_E^L L$. On localized morphisms the convention is
$$
 (u/\varpi^r)\otimes(v/\varpi^s)
   =(u\mathbin{\widehat\otimes}v)/\varpi^{r+s}.
$$
In particular the coefficient category here is the adic rationalization, with tensor computed by K-flat tensor followed by completion on integral representatives. The restriction of this construction to an exact bifunctor of Weil complexes is a separate property, not an axiom in this definition.

For Weil complexes $(K,\varphi_K)$ and $(L,\varphi_L)$, define their tensor Frobenius by the typed composite
$$
 \varphi_{K\otimes L}:
 \Phi_X^*(K\otimes_E^L L)
 \xrightarrow{\mu_{\Phi_X;K,L}}
 \Phi_X^*K\otimes_E^L\Phi_X^*L
 \xrightarrow{\varphi_K\otimes_E^L\varphi_L}
 K\otimes_E^L L.
$$
Here are the coefficient identifications and the comparison $\mu$. For $P_n=A/\varpi^n$, let $c_n:\Phi_X^{-1}(P_n)_X\xrightarrow{\sim}(P_n)_X$ be the constant-coefficient isomorphisms of [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image]. They are adjoint to the maps sending each constant section to itself [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Hence they preserve the residues of $\varpi$ and multiplication by those residues; their naturality for ring homomorphisms makes them commute with the quotient maps. The coefficient-ring isomorphism used for module pullback is
$$
 c:\Phi_X^{-1}A_X
 \xrightarrow{\sim}\varprojlim_n\Phi_X^{-1}(P_n)_X
 \xrightarrow{\varprojlim_n c_n}\varprojlim_n(P_n)_X=A_X.
$$
The first arrow uses preservation of limits by the inverse-image equivalence in that node. This $c$ preserves the scalar $\varpi$, as is checked after every projection to $(P_n)_X$.

With this ring map use the canonical comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] on integral representatives. More explicitly, write $H$ for the exact module transport induced by $\Phi_X^{-1}$ and $c$, before completion and rationalization. Choose flat-term K-flat representatives $U,V$ for $M,N$. Since the inverse-image equivalence preserves colimits and finite products, it preserves the balanced generators and relations defining sheaf tensor. Thus the canonical balanced map $HU^i\otimes_{A_X}HV^j\to H(U^i\otimes_{A_X}V^j)$ is an isomorphism; on local pure tensors it sends $u\otimes v$ to $u\otimes v$ after the coefficient identification $c$. Its inverse commutes with the two differentials and with direct-sum inclusions, so totalization gives inverse chain maps with the differential $d_U\otimes1+(-1)^i1\otimes d_V$. These represent the cited derived tensor comparison. The cited pullback statement ensures that $HU,HV$ are again flat-term K-flat representatives.

To complete this chain map, write $Q_m=[A_X\xrightarrow{\varpi^m}A_X]$ in degrees $[-1,0]$ as in [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion]. Applying $c$ in both degrees gives $HQ_m\cong Q_m$; it respects the transition maps since those are $\varpi$ in degree $-1$ and identity in degree $0$. Tensor the preceding degreewise maps with this identification to obtain isomorphisms of actual complexes
$$
 H(\operatorname{Tot}(U\otimes_{A_X}V)\otimes_{A_X}Q_m)
 \xrightarrow{\sim}
 \operatorname{Tot}(HU\otimes_{A_X}HV)\otimes_{A_X}Q_m.
$$
They commute with each strict tower transition because $c(\varpi)=\varpi$; no lifting of an arbitrary derived-category map to strict towers is being assumed. Apply the inverse-image equivalence to the product $B$ and the mapping-fiber complex $F$ in the completion definition: the product comparison is the map whose $m$-th component is the $m$-th inverse-image projection, and it commutes with $1-t$ by the transition identity just checked. On $F^i=B^i\oplus B^{i-1}$ use that comparison on both summands. It commutes with the differential $(x,y)\mapsto(d_Bx,(1-t)x-d_By)$, giving the comparison with completion. Rationalize this composite to obtain $\mu_{\Phi_X;K,L}$ in the displayed direction. The source's shorthand $\varphi_K\otimes\varphi_L$ denotes this composite.

proof.text: For wfSiteDerivedTensor_first, tensor the flat-term K-flat resolution V→D by P. The fixed-tensor lemma makes this a quasi-isomorphism. Compose its localization with the descent comparison on P,V.

source.place: First sentence: K-flat tensor and ambient coefficient model

proof.text: For wfTensorRepresentative_exists, specialize cochain tensor model rigidity to the completed coefficient sheaf. Its r gives the cochain comparison and its unique normalized e compares every other model, including the homotopy quotient and flatness identification.

source.place: First sentence: K-flat tensor and ambient coefficient model

proof.text: For wfRationalTensorHom_exists apply derived-completed tensor bilinearity to A→A_X and the Koszul reflector. It supplies linearity of ordinary tensor and completion, and the unique rational Hom action with numerator product and denominator sum; its laws define the rational bifunctor.

source.place: First sentence: K-flat tensor and ambient coefficient model

proof.text: For wfConstructible_complete, use the presentation witness in the integral constructible object. Canonical-completeness transport makes the actual intrinsic unit invertible for the stipulated list and representative. The normalized Koszul/quotient comparison identifies its tower unit.

source.place: First sentence: K-flat tensor and ambient coefficient model

proof.text: For wfPullbackCompletion_exists, use module pullback left adjoint to direct image, with completed coefficient map as specified. Apply the automorphism completion lemma to obtain preservation of completeness and the unique c_M with Hη_M;c_M=η_HM.

source.place: Second sentence: tensor Frobenius and completed coefficient transport

proof.text: For wfIsoPullback_complete, the unit square gives η_HM=Hη_M;c_M. If η_M is invertible, both factors are invertible, hence so is η_HM.

source.place: Second sentence: tensor Frobenius and completed coefficient transport

proof.text: For wfCompletePullback_linear apply completed-coefficient linearity with e=Φ_X: the inverse-image coefficient map is adjoint to identity on constant sections. Its scalar squares give additive A-linear complete pullback. Semilinear localization gives P̄(f/varpi^r)=P(f)/varpi^r.

source.place: Second sentence: tensor Frobenius and completed coefficient transport

proof.text: For wfRationalTensorPullback_exists, the preceding results supply B̄,P̄ and unit-square c. The statement's strict product/fiber map carries (u,0) to (Hu,0); uniqueness identifies it with c. Apply completed-tensor rational naturality with the Koszul reflector and canonical derived pullback/tensor comparison. It gives the unique normalized μ and its inverse. Compose μ with the tensor of the two Weil isomorphisms.

source.place: Second sentence: tensor Frobenius and completed coefficient transport

proof.text: For wfConstructibleInclusion_exists, the now-defined integral inclusion is A-linear since maps are unchanged. Semilinear localization with identity coefficient map gives base change on Hom. Every normalized functor agrees on integral arrows and inverses of scalar powers, hence on all fractions.

source.place: First sentence: K-flat tensor and ambient coefficient model

proof.text: For wfConstructiblePullback_obj evaluate this normalization on objects. Localization retains integral objects, whose underlying derived objects agree under coefficient transport; full-subcategory extensionality proves equality.

source.place: Second sentence: tensor Frobenius and completed coefficient transport

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q20-2c241c70f (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Re-delivery after the RETURN of 44e88368, which dropped base Steps 7-10. All ten steps of the base proof (the 'Original proof, retained verbatim' section) are now carried, with nothing shortened. Step 1 goes to the retained node lem-sf-completed-tensor-rational-naturality and Step 4 to the retained lem-sf-cochain-tensor-model-rigidity; both are byte-identical to the previous delivery and I re-checked them as true. Step 2 uses the existing fixed-K-flat-tensor, K-flat-resolution and site-descent nodes. Step 5 uses the existing lem-pur-semilinear-scalar-localization. Steps 3 and 6 are elementary. Steps 7-10 are four new statement-only nodes of 1700-1850 chars each: derived-completed-tensor-bilinearity, automorphism-completion-unit-comparison, completed-coefficient-pullback-linearity and constructible-canonical-completeness. The item proof is a ten-step assembly of 2618 chars. The four dropped proof_deps are restored in real steps, and proof_deps equals the union of the step uses. The order is fixed: B̄ (Step 3), completeness (Step 4), c (Step 5) and P̄ (Step 7) all come before rational naturality (Step 8), so every hypothesis of that node is now supplied. Mathematics checked. (1) Bilinearity: Hom groups in D(R) are A-modules through s, the reflector is A-linear by naturality of η and its Hom bijection, and β extends uniquely because Hom[1/p] = S⊗Hom. (2) For an automorphism, e^* is an exact equivalence that commutes with Koszul models and products, Re_* preserves completeness (Stacks 099N(1), read), so the unique c_M with Hη;c = η_H exists. (3) The scalar squares hold after each quotient projection by naturality of c_n, and a linear direct image makes its left adjoint linear. (4) Completeness transports through the scalar-preserving equivalence F; it does not depend on the representative (Q_m is bounded free and products are exact) or on the generators (the local condition depends only on J); the tower unit comes from the Koszul/quotient comparison. Small cases checked: p nilpotent, e = id, empty generator list, zero object. Stacks labels 06YS, 06YU, 0A0E, 099M, 099N, 03D7, 09A5 and 0H7J checked against tags. No cycle, no SGA, three kinds of search recorded per node, blueprint from = item with via []. The declared generic tool_uses are accepted. Advisory, not faults: (a) the linearity node repeats the automorphism node's clause that pullback preserves completeness, and its later splitter should cite that node; (b) the constructible-completeness hypothesis is the Lean presentation-witness form, whereas the DAG definition already demands intrinsic completeness, so the conclusion is still what Step 4 needs; (c) lem-sbc-completed-operations-linear-natural-exchange is related but not a duplicate.

blueprint_update.statement:

from a $K$-flat replacement of its first argument. For Weil complexes
$(K,\varphi_K)$, $(L,\varphi_L)$ the tensor Frobenius is
$\varphi_K\otimes\varphi_L$.
